clue.text: Trendy slating covers singular facility for nippers

parts.note: hip means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: the word for slating wraps around the letter, covering it

parts.note: flak is harsh criticism, a slating
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A fashionable but much-criticised service for small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nippers' looks like children, but a nip is a small tot of spirits, and this is what holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small measure of spirits, and this pocket flask is the container that carries such drinks.

clue.text: Base acquiring extra billion for its third scientist

indicators.note: the base word takes in a new letter in place of one of its own
the new letter replaces the third letter of the base word

parts.note: humble means lowly, base
B is the abbreviation for billion, added as an extra

explanation.surface: A modest scientist gets an extra billion in funding.
explanation.walkthrough: The third letter M of HUMBLE becomes B. Edwin Hubble was the US astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Hubble was an American astronomer who showed the universe is expanding.

clue.text: A class act

parts.note: per means a, as in a pound a day
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A classy performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' means each, as in 'per': ten pounds a head.
explanation.definitionFit: To act a play is to stage it, putting on a show for an audience.

clue.text: Fuel is spilled: dispatch United States rescue team?

indicators.note: spilled fuel is scattered, so the letters are rearranged
to dispatch is to get rid of, so the letter goes

parts.note: to aver is to state, so avers means states

explanation.surface: Fuel is spilled, so send in a US rescue squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' mixes up FUEL IS, and 'dispatch' sends away its U, so those letters give LIFES. 'United States' looks like one country but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: People who rescue others from drowning make up a rescue team, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Laying out article in feast: for example fish

parts.note: a spread is a lavish meal, a feast

indicators.note: the article goes inside the abbreviation for example

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
ling is a fish related to cod

explanation.surface: Laying out a feast, for instance some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretching a person or thing out flat with limbs extended is laying it out this way.

clue.text: Wriggle out of question framed by teacher at end of term

indicators.note: the teacher's title surrounds the question abbreviation like a frame

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word term is taken

explanation.surface: A pupil wriggles out of a question posed by the teacher at the end of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is just a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirm is to wriggle or writhe, often from embarrassment or discomfort.

clue.text: Yard one can use for bike

definitions.meaning: a courtyard enclosed by buildings, especially in a college
a four-wheeled off-road motorbike is called by this name

explanation.surface: A yard where you might ride a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle is a college courtyard, and a four-wheeled motorbike shares the short name.

clue.text: Annoying risk, turning crooked Cockney in

indicators.note: the word risk bends out of shape, its letters rearranged

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so at home becomes 'ome

explanation.surface: An annoying risk of a crooked Cockney turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' means at home; a Cockney (London working-class) speaker drops the H, giving OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome or irritating is annoying, causing vexation.

clue.text: Herb's stuff turning up or appearing in pickle

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

indicators.note: the word or shows up inside the word for pickle

parts.note: a jam is a pickle, a predicament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A herb's material comes up, or turns up in a pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives MAR from RAM. 'pickle' is a fix, a jam, not a preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic plant of the mint family is used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Pressure that goalie's under to make save

definitions.meaning: a unit of atmospheric pressure, and also the crossbar a goalkeeper stands beneath
save in the sense of except, as in all but one

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper under pressure has to make a save.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of pressure and the goal's crossbar share one short word, which also means except.

clue.text: Banger something you'd put out with water biscuit

parts.words: something you'd put out with water
parts.note: a blaze is extinguished with water
a cracker is a thin dry biscuit

explanation.surface: A sausage, something to dowse, and a water biscuit sound like a confused picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' suggests a British sausage, but here it is a noisy explosive; a water biscuit is a plain cracker.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is a loud explosive firework, the kind set off with a bang.

clue.text: Rarely can a car leave parking space reached from here

indicators.note: done rarely means done oddly, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: You can rarely leave a car in a parking space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking space' reads as one place for a car, but 'parking' gives P and 'space' is outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: This Florida spaceport is where NASA launches rockets into outer space.

clue.text: Shift something baby wears after examinations

indicators.note: the baby's garment follows the examinations

parts.note: looks are glances or inspections, examinations
a nappy is a British baby's diaper

explanation.surface: A baby's changing routine follows a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' is an imperative meaning hurry up. A NAPPY is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are informal commands to hurry, to get moving quickly.

clue.text: As well to carry gallons for drinking outside?

indicators.note: the phrase for as well holds the gallons letter, carrying it

parts.note: too means as well, also

explanation.surface: Asking a drinker to also carry gallons of drink outside.
explanation.walkthrough: A takeaway drink is ordered this way, to be drunk away from the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or drink ordered like this is taken away and consumed elsewhere, outside the shop.

clue.text: Fixes bunk with end of cord and sort of material

parts.note: pins fix or fasten things
bunk means nonsense, tripe

indicators.note: only the last letter of cord is taken

explanation.surface: Repairing a bunk bed with a piece of cord and some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed; it is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth woven with fine stripes, as in a banker's suit, is a sort of material.

clue.text: Picture unruly mob confronting jockey

indicators.note: an unruly mob is disorderly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to jockey for position is to vie or compete

explanation.surface: A painting of an unruly crowd facing a racehorse rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' means a film here, a cheap second feature; 'confronting' just puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture is an old word for a film, and this is a low-budget film.

clue.text: Fancy doorbell, perhaps: first class

parts.note: a doorbell is one example of something that chimes
A is the top grade, first class

explanation.surface: A first-class fancy doorbell.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a fantasy or wild imagining, and so is an illusory dream of that kind.

clue.text: One nervously marking winger?

parts.note: a birdwatcher twitches with excitement while ticking off a sighted bird, a winger

explanation.surface: A nervous defender marking a football winger.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests football defence; a 'winger' is a bird, and an obsessive birdwatcher ticks it off.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid birdwatcher who travels to see and tick off rare birds is given this slang name.

clue.text: American means to clean mug with powder and cheap paper

parts.note: ash is a fine powdery residue
a rag is a cheap, low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: Cleaning a cup with powder and old newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup but is slang for a face; the definition is the US name for a face cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: In US English a small cloth for washing the face is called this, a British flannel.

clue.text: Keep watch and piece of jewellery wrapped inside elastic

indicators.note: the jewellery is enclosed within the word for keep watch

parts.note: to spy is to keep watch secretly
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A watch and a ring wrapped in elastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep watch' reads like a timepiece to look after; it means look out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resilient that bounces back is elastic, full of bounce.

clue.text: Failure to make exclamations recalled when opening present

indicators.note: the exclamations go inside the present, opening it up

parts.note: now means the present time

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the exclamations are read backwards

parts.note: ohs are exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Gasps of delight remembered as a present is unwrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it is the present time. 'recalled' means called back, so the exclamations are read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fails to make an appointment or booking simply doesn't turn up.

clue.text: First of our chances at redemption is nigh — alas we blow it

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A preacher warns that our last chance of salvation is near, but we squander it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow it' sounds like ruining a chance; the definition is something you play by blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped wind instrument is played by blowing into it.

clue.text: Important to go on home, where one may have pressing needs

definitions.text: where one may have pressing needs

parts.note: key means important, crucial
a pad is slang for one's home

explanation.surface: Importantly, getting home where urgent needs can be met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go on' just joins the pieces. 'pressing needs' sounds urgent; it means buttons to press.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of buttons pressed to enter numbers or codes is where pressing happens.

clue.text: Rent rise by a quarter

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or rise
N, north, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A rent rise of a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' is the past participle of rend, meaning ripped, not money paid to a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as a past participle of rend means ripped apart or split.

clue.text: School leaver is put in row without old trophies

indicators.note: to school is to train or shape, so the letters are drilled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the old letter is removed from row

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A school leaver is placed in a line without the old prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without old' takes O from ROW, leaving RW; that and LEAVER and IS are rearranged together. 'put in' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cups and other trophies are commonly called this, especially in sport.

clue.text: Soundtrack Oscar for Born Free?

indicators.note: the sound of the word is what is entered, as heard

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright and wit

explanation.surface: The Born Free soundtrack wins an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the film award; it is the writer Wilde. 'Born Free' was a lion-cub film.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal born free in nature, not in captivity, is untamed and lives in its natural state.

clue.text: Having no majority party around can reduce scope of whip

indicators.note: the word for having no majority goes around the can

parts.note: a hung parliament has no single party with a majority
a tin is a can
to crop is to cut back or reduce

explanation.surface: A minority government trimming the reach of the party whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip' looks political, the chief whip, but it is a rider's whip; a HUNG parliament is one where no party has a majority.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short riding whip with a loop, carried in fox hunting.

clue.text: Rascal's disappearing act in effect

indicators.note: the act vanishes from the word for effect

parts.note: impact means effect or influence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rascal's vanishing trick that leaves its mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a mischievous child or little devil, a rascal.

clue.text: Middle Eastern venue had many tiers, the odd ones retracting

indicators.note: retracting means drawing back, so the chosen letters are read backwards
only the first, third, fifth letters and so on are taken

explanation.surface: A venue in the Middle East had many terraces, odd ones folding back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the odd ones' takes HDAYIR from 'had many tiers', and 'retracting' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Saudi Arabia, a Middle Eastern location.

clue.text: Happy-clapping is welcome!

parts.note: glad means happy
a hand is a round of applause, clapping

explanation.surface: A happy-clappy congregation is welcome!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy-clapping' reads as one hyphenated word for evangelical worship, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome someone effusively, shaking hands like a politician, is this verb.
